title: Trump to Award Top Science Medals to Musk, Nadella, Dell at Summit
excerpt: The president will present the National Medals of Science and Technology and Innovation at Thursday's White House 'Science: A New Golden Age Summit' — the first time he has awarded either honor.
body:
• President Trump will present the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su at Thursday's White House "Science: A New Golden Age Summit" — the first time he has awarded the honor.
  • Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the nation's highest honor for technological achievement.
  • The summit also serves as a showcase for the administration's plan to overhaul how federal scientific research funding is managed, with Energy Secretary Chris Wright and NASA chief Jared Isaacman slated to speak.
  • The medal for Musk marks his latest return to Trump's orbit months after his public rupture with the president and departure from his government efficiency role.

President Donald Trump will award the nation's highest honors for scientific and technological achievement to a slate of tech-industry titans on Thursday, presenting the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and AMD chief executive Lisa Su. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

The ceremony will take place at the White House's "Science: A New Golden Age Summit," and it marks the first time Trump has presented either medal across both of his administrations, according to Fox News Digital, which first reported the honoree list.

What the medals are

The National Medal of Science is the nation's highest honor for scientists and engineers, according to the US National Science Foundation's website. The National Medal of Technology and Innovation is the nation's highest honor for technological achievement, according to the US Patent and Trademark Office's website.

"The Trump Administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation."

— Liz Huston, White House spokesperson, to Fox News Digital

The summit's agenda

The summit is expected to bring together scientists and tech innovators to discuss how superintelligence and private-sector investment can accelerate scientific breakthroughs and strengthen US leadership in science and technology, Fox News Digital reported.

According to Reuters, Trump will separately speak at a White House event on scientific discovery on Thursday, where the administration will highlight its plan to overhaul how federal scientific research funding is managed and distributed. Tech adviser Michael Kratsios, who first released the plan in July, announced the event on X. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman are also slated to speak, according to an invitation seen by Reuters.

What the honoree list signals

The list is striking for who it centers: not university researchers or lab scientists, but the private-sector executives driving the AI hardware boom. Huang and Su run the two chipmakers at the heart of the artificial-intelligence buildout, while Dell's company supplies much of the data-center hardware behind it. The choices put the industry — not academia or government labs — at the center of the administration's science narrative.

Musk's inclusion is the most politically loaded. Once a close ally tasked with running the Department of Government Efficiency, Musk left the administration after a high-profile public rupture with the president earlier this year. The medal caps a steady reconciliation that has returned him to White House events, including last week's "Super Intelligence" luncheon with other tech CEOs.

Taken together, the ceremony doubles as policy theater: pairing a funding-overhaul pitch with the private-sector titans the administration wants to court. The message is that Washington's science strategy will run through Silicon Valley — with superintelligence, not federal grants, as the organizing theme.

Diaspora angle

Satya Nadella, who was born in Hyderabad and has led Microsoft since 2014, becomes one of the few Indian-born executives to receive a US national medal of this rank, joining a ceremony otherwise dominated by American-born tech founders.

What's next

The ceremony unfolds Thursday at the White House, where the spotlight will be on whether Trump uses the occasion to detail the research-funding overhaul Kratsios has been developing since July — and whether Musk attends and accepts the medal in person after months of on-again, off-again proximity to the president. Any executive orders or funding-reform specifics announced at the summit will be worth watching for their effect on universities and national labs.
